decision.explanation: Medal order does not matter, so choose 3 of the 10 contestants: \binom{10}{3}=\frac{10\cdot9\cdot8}{3\cdot2\cdot1}=120.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Out of the ten contestants in an Olympic event, how many possible groups of $3$ medalists are there, regardless of which medal they win?
after.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $10$ contestants, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those contestants for the medal positions, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different potential groups of medalists is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{C}_{3} & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!3!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}3!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{720}{6} \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

In general, the number of combinations of n objects taken r at a time is given by the formula nCr=n!(n−r)!r!.

10C3=10!(10−3)!3!=10!7!3!=10⋅9⋅8⋅7!7!3!=10⋅9⋅83⋅2⋅1=7206=120.

Question 2

Given any two points in a plane, there is a unique line that passes through both points. Given six points in a plane, what is the maximum number of unique lines that can be made using these points?

a
6
b
15
c
21

12
e

decision.explanation: The maximum occurs when no three points are collinear. Each pair determines a distinct line, so the number is \binom{6}{2}=6\cdot5/2=15.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given any two points in a plane, there is a unique line that passes through both points. Given six points in a plane, what is the maximum number of unique  lines that can be made using these points?
after.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $6$ points, so $n=6.$ We want to select $2$ of those points for each of the lines, so we have $r=2.$

Therefore, the maximum number of unique lines is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{6}{C}_{2} & =\frac{6!}{(6-2)!\,2!} \\  & =\frac{6!}{4!2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{30}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: There were $9$ chess players who took part in a chess tournament. How many games were played in the tournament if each player faced every other player exactly once?
after.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $9$ players, so $n=9.$ We want to select $2$ of those players for each of the matches, so we have $r=2.$

Therefore, the number of games is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{C}_{2} & =\frac{9!}{(9-2)!\,2!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{7!2!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}\cdot 2!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{72}{2} \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Stefany wants to draw a picture using $5$ colors from her $24$-color crayon box. In how many ways can she pick the $5$ colors?
after.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $24$ colors, so $n=24.$ We want to select $5$ of those colors for Stefany to draw her picture, so we have $r=5.$

Therefore, the number of choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{24}{C}_{5} & =\frac{24!}{(24-5)!\,5!} \\  & =\frac{24!}{19!5!} \\  & =\frac{24\cdot 23\cdot 22\cdot 21\cdot 20\cdot \cancel{19!}}{\cancel{19!}5!} \\  & =\frac{24\cdot 23\cdot 22\cdot 21\cdot 20}{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{5\,100\,480}{120} \\  & =42\,504.\end{aligned}

Question 5

Stefany wants to draw a picture using 5 colors from her 24-color crayon box. In how many ways can she pick the 5 colors?

a
2125
b
7962624
c
5100480
d
120
e
42504
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In general, the number of combinations of n objects taken r at a time is given by the formula nCr=n!(n−r)!r!.

There are 24 colors, so n=24. We want to select 5 of those colors for Stefany to draw her picture, so we have r=5.

Therefore, the number of choices is

24C5=24!(24−5)!5!=24!19!5!=24⋅23⋅22⋅21⋅20⋅19!19!5!=24⋅23⋅22⋅21⋅205⋅4⋅3⋅2⋅1=5100480120=42504.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Combinations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
content.problem: Stefany wants to draw a picture using $5$ colors from her $24$-color crayon box. In how many ways can she pick the $5$ colors?
content.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $24$ colors, so $n=24.$ We want to select $5$ of those colors for Stefany to draw her picture, so we have $r=5.$

Therefore, the number of choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{24}{C}_{5} & =\frac{24!}{(24-5)!\,5!} \\  & =\frac{24!}{19!5!} \\  & =\frac{24\cdot 23\cdot 22\cdot 21\cdot 20\cdot \cancel{19!}}{\cancel{19!}5!} \\  & =\frac{24\cdot 23\cdot 22\cdot 21\cdot 20}{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{5\,100\,480}{120} \\  & =42\,504.\end{aligned}
$$
